aliases.text: Pelvic Tilt Drill / Supine Pelvic Tilt

setup: Lie flat on your back on an exercise mat with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, about hip-width apart.
Rest your arms comfortably at your sides and allow your spine to settle into its natural resting curve, creating a small gap under your lower back.
steps: Engage your deep abdominal muscles and gently squeeze your glutes.
Roll your pelvis backward toward your ribcage, pressing your lumbar spine completely flat against the mat.
Hold the flattened, braced position for the intended duration while continuing to breathe shallowly.
Slowly relax the contraction and allow your pelvis to rock forward back to the neutral starting position.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you tilt your pelvis and flatten your back into the floor, then maintain calm, shallow breathing during any isometric hold.
cues: Crush the floor with your lower back

common_faults.fault: Pushing hard through the feet to lift the hips off the floor like a bridge.
common_faults.correction: Keep your hips in contact with the mat; the motion is a subtle rotational tilt of the pelvis, not a hip lift.

common_faults.fault: Holding your breath during the contraction.
common_faults.correction: Maintain relaxed breathing into the chest or sides while holding the abdominal brace.

common_faults.fault: Overusing the neck or tensing the shoulders.
common_faults.correction: Keep the upper body, neck, and shoulders completely relaxed against the floor.

precautions: Perform the movement gently and avoid forcing extreme lumbar flexion if you have acute disc symptoms.

name: Posterior Pelvic Tilt
summary: A supine core and mobility drill where the pelvis is tilted backward to flatten the lower back against the floor, activating the abdominals and glutes.
